analysis.investment_thesis: Birlasoft clears just one Magic Formula hurdle cleanly — ROCE of 21% passes the 20% threshold — but an earnings yield of ~6.5% (EBIT INR 698 Cr / EV ~INR 10,744 Cr) is unexciting, and a 9-year revenue CAGR of just 5.8% raises serious doubts about whether this is a genuinely 'good' business or merely an average one. The stock is fair value, not a bargain.
key_strengths: ROCE of 21% and near-zero debt (D/E 0.04, net cash ~INR 176 Cr) — asset-light balance sheet with no financial risk
Consistent OCF generation: INR 588 Cr in FY25, with FCF of INR 541 Cr — strong cash conversion (~105% of net profit)
Forward P/E of 17.6x and EV/EBITDA of 12x are reasonable for an IT services business with improving margins
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 5.8% over 9 years; top-line growth is weak and the company has not re-rated as a premium IT name
Operating income swung from INR 836 Cr (FY24) to INR 698 Cr (FY25) — earnings volatility undermines ROIC sustainability
Earnings yield of ~6.5% is too low for a Magic Formula conviction buy; the stock is not cheap enough to compensate for growth uncertainty
red_flags: Operating income declined YoY from INR 836 Cr (FY24) to INR 698 Cr (FY25) despite rising revenue — margin compression is a warning
9-year revenue CAGR of 5.8% barely beats inflation; this is not a high-quality compounder growing its competitive position
EBITDA trajectory shows a dip in FY23 (INR 569 Cr) after FY22 peak — not consistently expanding in a straight line
analysis.detailed_analysis:
EV of ~INR 10,744 Cr (mkt cap INR 10,920 Cr + debt INR 151 Cr – cash INR 327 Cr) against EBIT of INR 698 Cr gives an earnings yield of 6.5% — above the 6% floor but nowhere near the 12-15% that excites me. ROCE at 21% passes my threshold but just barely, and the FY25 operating income decline from FY24 levels is concerning. For the Magic Formula to fire, I need both legs strong simultaneously; here neither is compelling.

Birlasoft is a decent mid-tier IT services company — asset-light, debt-free, profitable — but it lacks the top-line velocity (5.8% 9-year CAGR) and pricing power of a Tier-1 or niche leader. At current prices it's approximately fairly valued. I'd revisit if earnings yield expanded to 10%+ on a sustained earnings recovery, but today there are better Magic Formula candidates.
